headline: InTelluric
speaker_note: Hero cover slide. Establish InTelluric as the technical co-author for consequential handoffs. Speaker notes: Early-stage technical founders, research teams, and startup operators approaching a critical development threshold — seeking investment, regulatory approval, grants, or patent protection. InTelluric is the technical co-author who catches the silent fault before it becomes the fatal flaw — making your vision structurally unambiguous and defensible to every reader who will never hear you explain it in person.

headline: The next handoff is the most dangerous threshold
speaker_note: Define the problem with force and precision: projects often fail not at conception, but when meaning must survive outside the founder's presence. This slide should make the vulnerability feel operational, not abstract.

headline: Ideas become vulnerable when they must defend themselves
speaker_note: Translate the founder narrative into a structural insight: a concept can be brilliant in conversation and still fail in independent reading. Make the contrast between founder narration and defensible record visually obvious.

headline: What InTelluric does
speaker_note: Present the service clearly as technical co-authorship and structural interrogation, not polish. Show the concrete artifact types and what gets improved in each engagement.

headline: Business model and go-to-threshold plan
speaker_note: Supply the missing investor-facing commercial structure: who buys, when they buy, how pricing works, and why this wedges into critical moments. Present inferred pricing as proposed, not validated.

headline: Why this wins now
speaker_note: Close with inevitability, positioning, and the ask. Frame InTelluric as the discipline serious builders adopt as scrutiny increases. Include a practical capital/use-of-proceeds ask because the deck must be complete.
